concepts.title: Classification of Polygons
concepts.definition: A polygon is a closed figure made of line segments meeting only at endpoints; polygons are classified by their number of sides - triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon - and by shape regularity, with regular polygons having all sides and angles equal.
concepts.key_idea: Count the sides to name the polygon; equal sides and angles make it regular.

concepts.title: Sum of the Measures of Exterior Angles of a Polygon
concepts.definition: Walking around any polygon and turning at every vertex makes one full revolution, so the exterior angles of every polygon total 360 degrees no matter how many sides it has; each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360 divided by the number of sides.
concepts.key_idea: One full turn of 360 degrees: exterior angles of any polygon always total 360.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh103.txt section 3.2 (sum of the measures of the exterior angles of a polygon)

solution_steps.explain: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon gets an equal share of 360 degrees.

concepts.title: Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon
concepts.definition: Diagonals from one vertex split an n-sided polygon into n minus 2 triangles, so the interior angles of any polygon sum to (n minus 2) times 180 degrees - 360 for quadrilaterals, 540 for pentagons and so on.
concepts.key_idea: Triangles inside carry the sum: n minus 2 of them times 180 degrees each.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh103.txt section 3.2 (sum of the measures of the interior angles of a polygon)

solution_steps.explain: The polygon splits into n minus 2 triangles.

concepts.title: Parallelogram Properties
concepts.definition: A parallelogram has parallel opposite sides and shows matched properties: opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal, and diagonals bisect each other; adjacent angles are supplementary, and a rectangle, rhombus and square are special parallelograms.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel sides force equal opposites and bisecting diagonals - the parallelogram package.

solution_steps.explain: Opposite sides must run parallel - the defining property.
Opposite sides and opposite angles come out equal; diagonals cut each other in half.
Right angles give a rectangle, equal sides a rhombus, both a square.
